info.raw:
Fair value is 10.5 (three dice, mean 3.5 each). I compared ask levels by expected profit per quote: the edge earned from noise traders minus the loss to informed traders who only buy when the sum is above the ask.

| Ask | Noise edge | Informed loss | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13.5 | 0.483 | 0.085 | 0.398 |
| 14.1 | 0.484 | 0.054 | 0.430 |
| 14.5 | 0.472 | 0.041 | 0.432 |
| 15.0 | 0.448 | 0.024 | 0.424 |
| 15.5 | 0.416 | 0.016 | 0.400 |

The best ask is about 14.5, four above fair value, and by symmetry the best bid is 6.5.

{"bid": 6.5, "ask": 14.5}

Settlement is 9 + die 3, so it is uniform on 10 to 15 and the public fair value is 12.5.

With one quote left and a flat position, I only need to maximise expected profit on this quote. An informed trader only buys when the value is above my ask and only sells when it is below my bid, so quoting outside the 10–15 range removes all informed losses. Beyond that, the noise-trader profit per side is 0.65 × d × P(noise > d) with standard deviation 4.4, which peaks at a distance d of about 3.3 from fair value (roughly 0.49 expected per side).

That gives an ask of 15.8 and a bid of 9.2.
